heroHeadline: SpaceX IFT-12 Cleared for Launch May 12 After Booster 19 Completes Full 33-Engine Static Fire
heroSubtitle: May 9: Booster 19 (Super Heavy V3) successfully completed a full-duration 33-engine static fire on May 7 — the follow-up test after an earlier abort — clearing Starship Flight 12 (IFT-12) for a May 12 opening window (22:30 UTC) extending through May 18. IFT-12 is the first flight of the completely redesigned Starship V3 architecture; its primary objectives include validating docking port and propellant-transfer hardware critical for Artemis III HLS qualification. The successful fire marks the most significant Starship HLS milestone since the April 1 Artemis II launch. At Kennedy Space Center, day 29 post-splashdown: Orion heat shield visual inspection at the Multi-Payload Processing Facility advances; formal Marshall X-ray scans remain scheduled for summer 2026. Artemis III SLS core stage integration continues in the VAB. Artemis II crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) continue physiological reconditioning at JSC. Artemis Accords remain at 67 nations (Paraguay 67th, May 7); Indonesia publicly weighing a potential signature.
